Amat etiam sanguinis de alieno vul-nere plenus, ad reversos è pugna accedere, narras, se cum suo periculo unū ex amicis servasse. ad ja-centem etiam tribules & populares introducit, qui cum visant: simul horum singulis narrat, se illum suis ipsius manibus in tē-torium portasse.
main_text.head: DE OLIGARCHIA, sive moribus optimatium.
main_text.p: Videri posit oligarchia, vehemens esse honorum cupiditas absque ullo lucri studio. Oligarchi sive optimatis hi sunt οὐκ ἐάσεις τὸν ἀν-θρωπον ὕπνῳ λαβεῖν πυκνὰ σημαίνων. ¶ αἵματος ἢ ἀνάπλεως ἀπὸ ἕ ἀλλοτρείας τραύ-μάτῳ[?], ἐπιλυγχάνειν τοῖς ἐκ τῆς μάχης ἐ-πανιέσι, ¶ διηγεῖσθαι ὡς κινδυνεύσας ὡς* σέσωσε τῶν φίλων. ¶ εἰσάγων πρὸς τὸν κατακείμενον σιφλό-*μυρῷ τὰς φιλέτας, τὸν δῆμον· ἐκ τέτων ἅμα ἑκάσῳ διηγεῖ-σθαι ὡς αὐτὸς αὐτὸν τῇ αὐτῆς χερσὶν ὅπι σκη-νὴν ἐκόμισεν.

page.notes: Greek marginal lines at top right are cut at their right and lower ends; the readings "Δήμευσ" and "Ἀπαν' ἐς κόρακας" are uncertain where marked, and the first Greek line is illegible in its middle. The "tē-" at the line end before "torium" is doubtful. The Greek notes are shown as side="right" because they stand in the right margin. Printed "vifant" is read as "visant" (long s as s). Asterisk marks in the right margin stand beside the lines where they appear; their note text is not visible on this part. The Greek words marked [?] and "Ὀξίεν", "σιφλό-", "φιλέτας", "τέτων" and "ὅπι" are uncertain readings. The large initial Δ is read as Ὀ of Ὀξίεν.
